title: Can a hidden parity equation change a marked three-parent join?
claim: Prove full scalar-table triple invariance for mixed-count serial growth or exhibit and minimize a reachable counterexample, then identify the least sufficient supplemental bond reading if a counterexample exists.
standard_statement: Does maximum information carried by all pairwise minimum cocircuit sizes of a serial binary-incidence parity presentation determine its marked three-element extension predicate?
prior_work: The preceding separator theorem proves equal allowed states imply identical triple verdicts but exhibits lost scalar state information already with legal triples at width 32.
completion_gate: Prove all-size scalar invariance, or exhibit an exact scalar collision with global minimality and a sharp sufficient extra observation. Keep any unabsolved obligation open.
source_contribution: The runtime sees the full bond-distance table, the proposed unordered triple, and the serial law.

validation.status: Passed for scoped results; global claim Partial

remaining_obligations: Decide whether changing a larger equation through one of the marked inputs, or a relation elsewhere affecting their ordinary witnesses, can flip a triple verdict under a full marked isometry.
If such a collision exists, certify reachable histories, every original entry, minimum width and the least sufficient supplemental reading.
conclusion: For the specified width-32 matrix the three mutual distances equal six exactly on its eight legal triples across every possible realization. The small-equation theorem, four-bit ineligibility and supplemental arity-five bound hold at all widths. The unrestricted scalar inverse remains open.
evidence_class: Uniform restricted theorems and exact per-table certificate, V1
failure_conditions: A reachable competitor matching every width-32 pair with a different triple verdict would refute the width-32 certificate.
A changed parity equation on at most four distinctions through a live input in scalar-equivalent sources would refute the short-equation theorem.
A pair with identical observations through arity five and opposite legal triples would refute the sufficient upper bound.
